subject: Default data retention: what Redwood keeps by default and how customers can request erasure
messages:
From: Sam Mitchell <sam.mitchell@brightwave.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightWave Legal <legal@brightwave.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: default retention/where our requests live

Hi Nikhil,

Quick question as we finalize the PO: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default for the hosted API? Specifically:
- Do you persist raw user prompts, model outputs, and streamed tokens?
- If so, how long are those retained and where (US/EU)?
- What’s the fastest path for BrightWave to get data erased if we need to (DSR/e-discovery)?

We need to include a short description in our security questionnaire. If you have a one-page summary or an internal PDF we can attach, that would help.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Mitchell
Head of Platform, BrightWave Analytics

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. I wanted to loop in Kim and Laura to ensure the answer covers compliance + product behavior. High level first-pass below; we’ll follow up with a one-page attachment and exact phrasing you can drop into your questionnaire.

Summary (short):
- By default on Redwood Hosted: we retain complete request/response records (the incoming prompt, model-generated final outputs) for 30 days for operational troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Streamed tokens (partial/fragmented streaming traces) are not stored persistently by default. They are only captured if a customer enables advanced debug logging or explicit request-level logging.
- Certain derivatives (embeddings, indexable artifacts) are retained longer by default for billing and cache-optimization — typically up to 365 days; those are surfaced in billing/export controls.
- Residency: requests for accounts created in the EU region are stored in EU data stores by default; US accounts stored in US. Dedicated/Private deployments follow customer-managed residency.
- Erasure: customers can request erasure via our DSR flow (support ticket + verification) — typical SLA 5 business days for hosted accounts without legal hold. For contracts requiring faster guarantees we offer contract-specific terms in Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: Kim/Laura — I attached a quick PDF draft (redwood-data-retention-summary-v1.pdf) and a short DSR checklist (dsr-request-steps.txt).

N

Nikhil — suggested edits to keep us consistent with policy and avoid overpromising:

Proposed precise wording for Sam and legal:
- Default capture: Hosted accounts record request metadata and final model outputs by default for an operational retention window of 30 days. This capture includes the submitted prompt text and the final model-generated response.
- Streamed tokens: transient streaming frames are not persisted in the production telemetry store unless explicitly enabled by the customer ("debug logs" feature). If enabled, debug logs are retained under the same window unless a customer requests a different setting.
- Derivatives and indexes: artifacts created for indexing/embedding (used for retrieval or caching) are retained up to 365 days by default; customers can opt for shorter windows via the Console or API.
- Residency: data created by requests is stored in the geographic region tied to the account by default (US or EU). For added compliance we provide Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) which keep all artifact storage under customer control.
- Erasure & DSR: we provide a documented DSR flow (support ticket + identity verification + eDiscovery export if requested). Standard hosted erasure SLA: 5 business days for normal erasure; exceptions for legal hold or export requests may add time.

I also recommend calling out the following in your questionnaire: whichever retention window is chosen we can document a contractual SLA for Dedicated seats.

If you want, I can convert this to a 2-para blurb for your security questionnaire.

K

Sam — attaching the short summary and a DSR checklist (attached). Below is the exact blurb you can paste into your questionnaire.

Paste-ready answer for security questionnaire:
"Redwood Hosted — default data retention: By default Redwood retains the original submitted prompt text and the model's final generated outputs for an operational window of 30 days to support debugging, quality monitoring, and fraud detection. Partial streaming frames (in-flight tokens) are not persisted in production stores unless a customer opts in to debug-level logging. Derivative artifacts used for retrieval (embeddings, caches, indexes) are retained up to 365 days by default; customers can shorten retention via the Redwood Console or API. Data residency is tied to the customer's account region (US or EU); Dedicated and Private deployments provide customer-managed residency. Customers may request erasure via Redwood's DSR workflow (support.redwood-inference.com/kb/data-retention). Standard hosted erasure SLA is 5 business days for accounts not under legal hold."
